newsitem.title: JAPAN: Jellyfish force Japan nuclear reactor to cut output.
newsitem.headline: Jellyfish force Japan nuclear reactor to cut output.

text.p: Environmentalists who have unsuccessfully tried for years to put the brakes on Japan's massive nuclear power programme might take a lesson from humble sea creatures -- jellyfish, which on Tuesday forced a coastal reactor to slash its output.
A power firm in western Japan temporarily halved power output at a 820,000-kilowatt nuclear reactor after a water cooling intake pump was blocked by a school of jellyfish, a company spokesman said.

Operations of the two purifiers at the pump were automatically halted when jellyfish clogged them, forcing the utility firm to lower power production at the reactor to 440,000 kilowatts, a Chugoku Electric Power Co spokesman said.
"This is the first time in 20 years we have had this many jellyfish," he said, noting that small numbers of jellyfish appear near the plant annually as sea waters warm up with the approach of summer.

The utility started bringing operating rates back up again after removing the jellyfish, which took about 90 minutes, and the reactor was expected to reach full capacity by the end of the day, the spokesman said.
Japan depends on nuclear power for about one-third of its energy needs.
